We're supposed to be principled people, are we not.

And to be clear, I'm not putting this dumbass knitting site in the same league as Google or Twitter or Facebook.

I do still think we're treading on dangerous ground when we start to legislate what they can or can't censor on their own platforms, too.

On the other hand, I think the "public square" argument is strong against social media and search engines. I just worry how "public square" may be defined at some point later, however. As in, we might up forcing a "fairness doctrine" on ourselves later as a result, and it will be anything but fair.

Between the "public square" argument and the fact that these tech giants are in fact monopolies, I think good legislation combined with anti-trust cases can fix some of this.

I'm just saying that a careful approach needs to be made here, because if this is done wrong, it will bite us in the ass later in ways we haven't even thought of yet.
